title: wt sweep --yes --json
description: What a wt sweep did, item by item. Printed by `wt sweep --yes --json [--expect <token>]` as the only thing on stdout, also when a handled SIGINT or SIGTERM ends the run. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows: minor for an added field or enumeration value, patch for wording.

token.description: The token of the plan this run carried out; null when it stopped before one was made, or there was nothing to do.

outcome.description: done: every item to remove or delete went. refused: nothing was removed or deleted. partial: some went, some did not. interrupted: a signal ended the run.

error.description: Why the run stopped before touching anything: an --expect that no longer holds, the fetch, not the main checkout.

category.description: Its part of the plan, as in the sweep-plan schema.

result.description: removed: the worktree and its branch are gone. deleted: the branch is gone. kept: left as it was, on purpose. failed: tried and not finished; worktreeRemoved and branchDeleted say what did happen. notRun: the run ended before it. interrupted: the one a signal caught.

reason.description: Why, for everything but removed and deleted.

restoreCommand.description: When the branch was deleted: the git command, as an argv, that puts it back at the commit it was at.
